 Order

This second bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Criminal Complaint case No. 556/2023(RCT) pending before First Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC.

entities.text: First Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 22.12.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 42110/2023.
2.

As per case of prosecution, Smt. Ramlata Sharma submitted a private complaint before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Morena inter-alia alleging that Vinod Sharma s/o Harnaryan Sharma has no agricultural land.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He has secured KCC loan showing himself to be holder of agricultural land.
Further, he has secured crop insurance and relief amount from the Government without there being any land in his name.
Applicant has forged land records to secure KCC loan and crop insurance amount.

Smt. Ramlata Sharma was examined under Section NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19508 2 MCRC-22593-2024 200 of the Cr.P.C.

Thereafter, learned Trial Court vide order dated 05/04/2023 took cognizance for offence punishable under Sections 420, 468, 467,
471 and 120-B of the IPC against applicant Dev Prakash Sharma and others.
Summons and bailable warrants were issued to secure presence of the applicant.
Applicant is apprehending his arrest.

sentences.text:
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application,
submits that the Trial Court merely on the basis of complaint and statement of complainant recorded under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C proceeded to take cognizance for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC against the applicant.
There is no complaint from any bank with regard to forgery of documents or securing KCC loan by cheating.
The complaint is filed due to political rivalary over election of Sarpanch.

The allegation that KCC loan was secured by the applicant without holding any land in his name, stands falsified in view of Khasra Entries showing land at survey No. 1053/2 recorded in name of applicant since 2011 till 2024.
Learned counsel further submits that the Revenue Authorities are maintaining these Khasra entries in computer record.
The Revenue Authorities have not found these entries as forged or manipulated.
Even the bank has not found any forgery, therefore, no complaint is made by the bank.
Learned Trial Court without considering these aspects of the matter proceeded to issue process against applicant who is Sarpach of Naugaon.
He has social status.
Jail incarceration would bring social disrepute and hardship to the applicant.
The matter relates to documentary evidence.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by the applicant.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion.
Trial would take time to conclude.

It was also argued that co-accused Vinod Sharma, who is also similarly situated, had been granted second anticipatory bail on 01.04.2024, after dismissal of the first application of the applicant, thus, under this changed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19508 3 MCRC-22593-2024 circumstances, the second application also needs to be allowed.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for State ably assisted by objector/complainant vehemently opposes anticipatory bail application and submits that complainant has done her public duty to inform about misdeeds by applicant and others.

SDO(P), Banmore, District Morena conducted enquiry and found that the Revenue entries made in computer record are not substantiated by the evidence of concerned Halka Patwari, therefore, these entries are forged.
Taking benefit of the forged entries

,
applicant has secured KCC loan.
On consideration of report of concerned SDO(P), learned Trial Court took cognizance against the applicant.
Therefore, applicant may not be extended benefit of anticipatory bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commencing on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.

7. Accordingly, it is directed that in the event of arrest of applicant, applicant Dev Prakash Sharma shall be released on bail in relation to Criminal Complaint case No. 556/2023 (RCT) pending before J.M.F.C, Morena (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/ Investigation Officer making arrest, for compliance with the following conditions:-

8. This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the precondition of bail, it shall become ineffective without reference to the Court.
9. The trial Court shall get these conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
